description:
Software and retained results for Walsh-coded and negotiated targets for motor imagery EEG decoding: a controlled evaluation of accuracy and confidence, by Salih Çolakoğlu, Mustafa Onat and Nuri Korhan. The accompanying manuscript is being prepared for IEEE Access review; this software record is not a journal publication.

The original 1,415 CSP–CNN/EEGNet fits and 800 EEGNet prediction files are retained. Added studies comprise 1,350 Lee2019 EEGNet test records and 54 classical references, a separate 1,350-model 80/20 calibration control, and 1,320 later-day SHU tests from an architecture/output comparison. The completed 270-fit W4 ungated-anchoring control, its independently audited results, and its fresh execution path are included. Its two exploratory accuracy comparisons remain separate from the earlier five-comparison family. Participant groups, information budgets and statistical families remain separate.

Portable prepared-input training tools, scientific source snapshots and no-training prediction-verification commands are provided. Raw EEG recordings, prepared signal caches, model checkpoints and private correspondence are not included. The original code and stored-results archive retain their bytes.

MIT applies to software. The authors' original documentation and generated numerical results use CC BY 4.0. Original BNCI labels retain CC BY-ND 4.0, Lee/OpenBMI labels retain CC0-1.0, and SHU labels retain CC BY 4.0. The primary software-license field does not override this mixed scope. See LICENSING.md, DATA_ATTRIBUTION.md and third-party notices.

The v2.1.0 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23290274 identifies the older archive only. This version is cited independently. The findings do not establish universal superiority, prevention of forgetting, or clinical readiness.
